title: The PTWC gauge-based score gain can reverse with 26 higher coastal categories in 123 test pairs
abstract: A prior PTWC study converted issued tsunami categories to gauge-maximum probabilities. We reproduce its 56.85% ranked probability score gain in 123 test pairs from 2021-2026. We then allow each true coastal category to equal or exceed its gauge category. The sharp mean score difference, conversion minus literal category, ranges from -0.43192 to +0.37099. The gain can reverse with 26 higher coastal categories, or with changes within two earthquakes. A one-category limit per pair needs 29 changed pairs. For 15 pairs with at least 11 gauge records, the conversion is worse for every allowed coastal assignment: the difference is +0.16868 to +0.44381. One of eight event deletions removes this robust sign. We prove a simple turning-point rule for ordinal score differences and give exact pair, event, and category-crossing budgets. These are fixed-sample sensitivity bounds, not estimates of missed waves. We reuse the parent records and do not measure new coastal peaks.

display.caption: Exact score bounds for coastal categories at or above recorded gauge categories. Dots show the gauge scores. Positive values favor the literal comparator. These are fixed-sample bounds, not confidence intervals.
Sharp upper score differences as the allowed number of changed pairs, events, or category crossings increases. Each budget has its own attaining assignment.

citations.reason: Frozen PTWC pairs and conversion-table comparison. The gain at gauges is reproduced; its transfer to coastal maxima is bounded.
Earlier campaign method for sharp missed-positive Brier score budgets; extended here to ordinal coastal outcomes.
